newsitem.title: USA: Total Entertainment changes proposed IPO terms.
newsitem.headline: Total Entertainment changes proposed IPO terms.

text.p: Sports restaurant company Total Entertainment Restaurant Corp changed the proposed terms of its initial public offering to raise slightly less than when it first filed to go public.

The company will raise $18.9 million in gross proceeds by selling 2.1 million shares for $8.50 to $9.50 each. In its initial filing, it planned to offer two million shares for between $9 and $11 each. That would have raised $20 million.
The deal is tentatively slated for the week of June 14, 1997, according to lead underwriter Montgomery Securities.
The shares are proposed to trade on the Nasdaq under the symbol "TENT". After the offering, there would be roughly 10 million shares outstanding.

The company owns and operates 12 restaurants -- nine Bailey's Sports Grilles three Fox & Hound restaurants in Arkansas, Indiana, North Carolina, South Carolina, Tennessee and Texas. Before 1997, the two restaurant chains were operated as separate companies. Only three of the restaurants have been operating for more than three years.
The restaurants combine full menus and full-service bars with sports entertainment, billiards and late-night dining and entertainment, according to the company's prospectus.

Total Entertainment plans to open five locations in 1997, 20 in 1998 and an additional 20 in 1999. It has said it plans to incur substantional costs over the near term in connection with the expansion plans.
